items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: Eddie, Eddie is an original. Yeah. In a sense, he, he certainly created a style of his own. His playing is distinctive. He's an extremely talented man.

ctx.x: And, if you had to name a single famous New Orleans saxophone player, you could name one, I'd say. Eddie Miller, of course.

Eddie, Eddie is an original. Yeah. In a sense, he, he certainly created a style of his own. His playing is distinctive. He's an extremely talented man. And probably, if you wanted to hear his clarinet playing, I don't know, Leon Rapolo's playing real well. But, it's my feeling probably that Eddie would probably play more like him than anybody. If you listen to some of the quirky courses that he made that would have even credited to him, they would amaze you. Have you heard the Bud Brown record with Eddie? Oh, yeah.
I got that. I guess Bud gave it to me on, either him or the guitar player. I mean, you know.

items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: And, that is the year that the Ben Pollack Band played Club Forrest in New Orleans. And, Aidy Miller had just joined the band.

ctx.x: Just so I can see what's happening here. I'm trying to figure out how to prop it out. That's okay. Go ahead. It's facing you.

Okay. There was a music store in 3-4th, formed by Bubba Broyles. Bubba was a trumpet player, and he'd been playing with the local bands there. And, he was a great friend of Mr. A.J. LaCoste, who was a power with the Whirland Organization. A.J. was the management of the band department. He organized school bands all over Mississippi and Louisiana. He was a tremendous man. But, Bubba and LaCoste asked me to come to New Orleans, that I would have some kind of a job. I had, I tried to go back to playing and played…
You have to be careful. Now you were talking about Leslie Nurse, was his name?
